## Summary

Root cause confirmed: `PROGRESS.md` was git-tracked, and every worker branch (via `veridian-task.py`'s `cmd_create` + `worker-entrypoint.sh`'s protocol instruction) overwrites it with its own narrative — guaranteeing a conflict whenever two task branches diverged and merged back close in time (PR12, PR23, PR24, PR27 all hit exactly this).

**Fix**: untracked `PROGRESS.md` from git (`git rm --cached`) and added it to `.gitignore` with a comment explaining why. It stays a local, per-workspace scratch file — `parse_progress_md()`, `cmd_checkpoint`, and `cmd_resume_context` in `veridian-task.py` all already read it straight off disk, never via git, so nothing else changed. No edits to any task lifecycle script logic.

**Proof**: cloned the repo to a scratch dir, branched two throwaway branches off the fixed commit, each wrote different content to their local `PROGRESS.md` and committed an unrelated marker file — `git add PROGRESS.md` was refused as ignored on both, so neither commit touched it. Merging both into an integration branch succeeded with zero conflicts. Scratch clone and throwaway branches were local-only and deleted after; nothing pushed.

**Verified**: `veridian-task.py resume-context` still works correctly post-fix.

PR opened and mergeable: https://github.com/FChecklist/claude-control/pull/28. Task checkpointed as `pending_review`.
